newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence plunges - National Bank.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence plunges - National Bank.

text.p: The festive spirit seems to have eluded New Zealand businesses, with only a net seven percent of respondents to the National Bank's December business confidence survey expecting an improvment in overall conditions in the next 12 months, the bank said on Thursday.
This was down from 20 percent in November.
"The decline in confidence is despite interest rates having continued to fall," National Bank said.
The decline was spread across all sectors excluding construction. The largest decline was in the agriculture sector, with a net 29 percent of repsondents expecting tougher times ahead.
The service sector also suffered a blow, with only a net 17 percent now expecting better times compared to 32 percent in November, the bank said.
Confidence in the retail sector had also declined to a net 14 percent expecting improved conditions, from 27 percent.
National Bank said these patterns were similar across respondents' own activity outlook. A net 25 percent anticipated an increase in their own activity levels, down from 31 percent in November.

"The construction sector is unique in its expectations of an increase in activity. A net 33 percent of construction respondents now expect to be busier, up from a net 7 percent expecting a decline as recently as July," the bank said.

It said interest rate expectations continued to point downward, with a net 50 percent of respondents anticipating a decline. Although down from a net 65 percent last month, National bank said the direction of the sentiment remained undoubted.
The outlook for profits remained positive, but only just.

"A net eight percent of repsondents expect a rise in profit, down from 13 percent last month. This decline is most prevalent in the agriculture sector where a net 34 percent of respondents expect an outright decline, back to near its all-time low."
Investment intentions were also down considerably, with 11 percent expecting to increase investment over the next 12 months, compared to 17 percent last month. The decline was across all sectors.

"Inflation expectations have nudged upward to 2.8 percent for the year ahead. This is disappointing in the sense that actual underlying inflation is 2.3 percent, with the likelihood that this will decline further over the next few quarters," said National Bank.
Employment intentions had deteriorated, with a net three percent expecting to increase employment, down from eight percent last month.
Pricing intentions remained similar to November, with a net 10 percent anticipating a rise in their product prices over the next three months.
National Bank noted that the survey results were gathered before some key policy announcements, among these the December endorsement of easier monetary policy by the Reserve Bank.
